govt_capex.evidence: Cables business (power/telecom) is exposed to government infrastructure and telecom rollout demand, but no revenue percentage tied to government capex was found.

International growth outpaced domestic, but no explicit China+1/API-sourcing diversification narrative was found attributed to Emcure specifically.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs/KSMs/APIs exists (~Rs 6,940cr outlay, 4-10% incentive on incremental sales), but no source confirmed Emcure specifically as a beneficiary or disclosed a revenue contribution from it.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is ENA (extra neutral alcohol) sourced from grain/molasses, not crude-oil linked; no raw material cost percentage tied to crude oil disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found; APL Apollo is a predominantly domestic-focused structural steel tube manufacturer serving Indian infrastructure, housing and irrigation demand.

rural.evidence: Search results reference rural/agricultural irrigation (drip & sprinkler) and rural housing as demand drivers for pipes historically, but no specific rural revenue % was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Government infrastructure capex (roads, irrigation, urban housing) is cited generally as a demand driver for steel tubes/pipes; no specific % of revenue from government-funded projects disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company uses short-term commercial paper/working-capital debt (e.g., ₹200cr CP at ~6.1%, ICRA A1+ rated) for working capital; specific % of total debt that is floating-rate was not disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is Hot Rolled Coil (HRC) steel, not a crude-oil-linked input; HRC price volatility is cited as the key margin risk, not crude oil.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company is overwhelmingly a domestic-revenue (INR) business; no material USD revenue exposure or hedging policy details found in sources searched.

pli_scheme.evidence: A broader ₹6,322 crore PLI scheme for specialty steel exists industry-wide (FY24-FY28), but no confirmation was found that APL Apollo itself is an approved/participating beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Not applicable - ABDL is a domestic IMFL (Indian Made Foreign Liquor) business; exports are described only as a nascent, selective expansion effort (e.g., planned CY26 launch of Zoya/Arthaus brands abroad), with no China+1/diversification framing.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural revenue % disclosed. Premium & Above (P&A) segment brands accounted for ~50% of IMFL value and ~40% of volume in FY25, implying the remaining mainstream/economy brands (e.g., Officer's Choice) skew toward semi-urban/rural markets, but this is inferred, not stated.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable to this business (alcobev, not capex/infrastructure linked); company's revenue is instead tied to state excise regimes and distributor relationships (e.g., dependence on state corporations like TSBCL in Telangana).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Interest expense rose ~7.3% YoY in FY25; credit rating upgraded to IND AA-/IND A1+ by India Ratings; specific % of borrowings on floating rates not disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are grain (corn/barley, largely imported from the USA), sugarcane/molasses (Brazil, Thailand), Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), and glass/PET packaging. PET packaging has a petrochemical (crude-linked) input, but no % of raw material cost tied to crude oil was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is almost entirely domestic (INR); however grain/molasses imports create USD-denominated cost exposure. No specific hedging policy or USD revenue % found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to the alcobev/IMFL sector; no beneficiary status found.

china_plus_one.evidence: "China+1 strategy and global supply chain diversification efforts are further enhancing India's role as a trusted global manufacturing hub... Divi's has started highlighting instances of conversion of RFQs to pilot projects/contracts, although large financial benefits will still take time to materialise" (3-5 years). Company is positioned as a direct beneficiary as global drugmakers diversify away from China for API/KSM sourcing, and has announced PLI-supported capacity in API segments where Chinese pricing had made domestic investment previously unviable.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's carries minimal debt — total borrowings comprise only working-capital limits (cash credit/overdraft), lease liabilities and LC-backed creditors; capex is funded via internal accruals; interest coverage ratio reported extremely high (~1,394x), implying negligible floating-rate term-debt exposure.

crude_exposure.evidence: Solvents (petrochemical/crude-oil-derived) are cited as a recurring source of raw-material cost pressure; geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia added sourcing risk, prompting a shift to a 3-month rolling inventory strategy. Specific % of raw material cost linked to crude oil not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company undertakes hedging transactions as and when required; enters contracts with major clients at fixed exchange rates with currency-fluctuation impact shared between both parties; imports (~49% of raw material consumption in FY25) provide a natural hedge; company also manages exposure by maintaining a balanced geographic revenue mix to match FX-denominated liabilities and earnings.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were 88% of gross sales in FY25 (vs 87% in FY24), predominantly USD/EUR-denominated (Europe 56.5%, North America 16.2%).

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's has announced PLI-supported capacity expansions in API segments where Chinese pricing had previously made domestic investment unviable, under India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates (~₹6,940 crore outlay, running through FY2029-30). Specific % revenue benefit not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Export orders from Europe and Asia for retrofits and new builds grew amid a China+1 supply-chain shift"; export and deemed-export order inflow was ~67-68% of total FY25 order inflow (record order inflow of ₹1,479 crore, up 41% YoY), with export growth outpacing weak domestic order growth (~4% YoY).

govt_capex.evidence: Products (steam turbines, generators) serve sectors with significant government/PSU capex exposure (thermal/renewable power, railways, steel, oil & gas), but no explicit % of revenue from government-funded capex was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported as substantially debt-free, with capex (e.g., ~₹140 crore) funded entirely from internal accruals; D/E ratio reported around ~1.7%, implying minimal floating-rate debt exposure.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are copper and electrical steel (not crude-oil-linked); high inventory buildup of copper and steel impacted FY25 operating cash flow; sharp copper price increases flagged as a margin risk.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/deemed-export order inflow was ~67-68% of total FY25 order inflow, implying material foreign-currency (largely USD/EUR) revenue exposure; specific hedging policy and USD % of actual revenue (vs. orders) not disclosed in sources found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of TD Power Systems participating in any PLI scheme; industrial steam turbines/generators are not a PLI-covered product category in sources reviewed.

Order backlog CY2024 ₹9,380-9,400 cr (+12% YoY), orders ₹13,079 cr.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India is described as 'almost debt-free' with only ~₹115 cr in settled borrowings as of the reporting balance sheet — negligible floating-rate liability exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Cupid's participation in a PLI scheme; company's scale (~₹200-250 cr revenue) is likely below typical PLI (e.g. textiles) minimum turnover thresholds (₹200-600 cr).

china_plus_one.evidence: Aegis is a domestic India-focused oil/gas/LPG logistics and terminal infrastructure business (Mumbai, Pipavav, Haldia, Kandla) serving PSU oil marketing companies (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) and industrial clients; no export or China+1 relevance found.

govt_capex.evidence: Aegis's LPG and liquid terminal business is structurally tied to PSU oil marketing companies (IOC/BPCL/HPCL) for bottling-plant feed volumes (e.g. BPCL-HPCL Uran-Chakan pipeline); no explicit revenue % tied to government capex disclosed. crude_exposure.evidence: Company is explicitly exposed to Brent crude price fluctuations, which affect costs, trading margins and storage demand in its LPG sourcing/trading segment (a large, lower-margin revenue contributor per rating agency commentary); no specific % of raw material/COGS tied to crude was disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Both Aegis Logistics and Aegis Vopak Terminals reportedly use derivative instruments (incl. cross-currency interest rate swaps) to manage interest-rate and forex risk, per third-party summaries.
inr_exposure.evidence: LPG procurement/trading is import-linked and internationally priced (typically USD/Saudi CP-linked), implying FX cost exposure, though explicit disclosed percentage not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Logistics/storage/distribution business; no applicable PLI scheme identified.

EMMVEE.report_year: FY2024-25 (per RHP prospectus filed ahead of Nov 2025 IPO)

china_plus_one.evidence: Company growth is linked to India's ALMM (Approved List of Models and Manufacturers) policy and Basic Customs Duty on imported solar modules, which favor domestic manufacturers over Chinese/imported modules within India's own market (import substitution rather than export-oriented China+1). Emmvee holds ALMM List-I status and expects List-II benefits from June 2026. However, ~55% of raw material purchases (silicon-related) are still sourced from China, indicating continued upstream China dependency even as downstream module sales substitute for Chinese imports domestically. Export revenue itself is minimal (0.87% of FY25 revenue) with presence in 19 countries (Europe, US, Africa).

govt_capex.evidence: Growth tied to government PLI ('National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules', sector outlay ~₹24,000 cr across Tranche I & II) and Make in India solar policy rather than direct government infrastructure capex.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total consolidated borrowings ~₹2,032 cr as of June 2025, largely IREDA loans for TOPCon manufacturing capacity; a further ~₹3,300 cr of new debt has reportedly been tied up (sub-8% interest cost) to fund a ~₹5,500 cr capacity expansion. No explicit fixed/floating split disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cost of materials consumed was ~67.6% of revenue in FY26 (₹3,412 cr vs. revenue ₹5,050 cr), driven by polysilicon, wafers, EVA encapsulant, copper and aluminum; some inputs (e.g. EVA encapsulant) are petrochemical/crude-oil derivatives but no explicit % tied specifically to crude oil was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is minimal (0.87% in FY25), but a major raw material component (wafers, polysilicon, largely imported, ~55% from China) creates FX cost-side exposure on the import/payables side rather than revenue side.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company is described as benefiting from India's PLI scheme for high-efficiency solar PV modules and 'Make in India' incentives, plus ALMM List-I/List-II eligibility enabling participation in government and government-assisted solar projects/DCR-linked schemes. Specific PLI-linked revenue or incentive-income percentage was not found in available sources.
